KNOWN_IMAGE_GENERATION_BASELINE.description: An enum of all the image generation baselines.
KNOWN_IMAGE_GENERATION_BASELINE.title: KNOWN_IMAGE_GENERATION_BASELINE

KNOWN_IMAGE_SAMPLERS.description:
The samplers that are known to the API.

(k_lms, k_heun, DDIM, etc)

The members below `DDIM` are the extended solvers, which only bridges new enough to render them
are offered. They carry the image backend's own spelling rather than the `k_` prefix of the
k-diffusion block, because they are backend-native solvers rather than k-diffusion samplers.

The members below `sa_solver` complete the backend's non-`_gpu` solver list. The `_gpu` variants
are deliberately absent: they differ from their counterparts only in which device draws the noise,
which is a worker-side concern rather than a request-side choice. Like the block above them these
names are shared letter for letter with the backend.
KNOWN_IMAGE_SAMPLERS.title: KNOWN_IMAGE_SAMPLERS

KNOWN_IMAGE_SCHEDULERS.description:
The schedulers that are known to the API.

(normal, karras, exponential, etc)

`align_your_steps` and `gits` are not schedules the backend names alongside the others: they are
sigma generators supplied by separate nodes, and each is only defined for a subset of the known
baselines. See
[`SCHEDULER_BASELINE_APPLICABILITY`][horde_sdk.generation_parameters.image.constraints.SCHEDULER_BASELINE_APPLICABILITY]
for where they may be requested.
KNOWN_IMAGE_SCHEDULERS.title: KNOWN_IMAGE_SCHEDULERS

KNOWN_SAMPLER_SOLVER_TYPES.description:
Every `solver_type` value any sampler accepts.

No sampler accepts all of them. The `midpoint`/`heun` pair and the `phi_1`/`phi_2` pair belong to
different solver families; see
[`SamplerConstraints.solver_type_choices`][horde_sdk.generation_parameters.image.constraints.SamplerConstraints.solver_type_choices].
KNOWN_SAMPLER_SOLVER_TYPES.title: KNOWN_SAMPLER_SOLVER_TYPES

PublishedCostBasis.description:
Represents what each published cost figure is, and which of them a request is charged against.

Served as bare numbers the measured ratios would read like prices. They are one card's evidence that
the evaluation counts are right, and this block says so.

authoritative_field.description: Names the field a request is priced and time-budgeted on.
authoritative_field.title: Authoritative Field

authoritative_note.description: What that field counts, and where it is read from.
authoritative_note.title: Authoritative Note

measured_cost_ratio_provenance.description: The provenance both measured ratio columns carry.

measured_cost_ratio_source.description: Filename of the measurement artifact both ratio columns were read from.
measured_cost_ratio_source.title: Measured Cost Ratio Source

measured_cost_ratio_note.description: How the ratios were derived, and why they corroborate the authoritative field rather than replace it.
measured_cost_ratio_note.title: Measured Cost Ratio Note

measured_cost_ratio_sdxl_note.description: The model and resolution the stable_diffusion_xl column was taken on, and how to read it.
measured_cost_ratio_sdxl_note.title: Measured Cost Ratio Sdxl Note

measured_cost_ratio_sd15_note.description: The model and resolution the stable_diffusion_1 column was taken on, and the bias it carries.
measured_cost_ratio_sd15_note.title: Measured Cost Ratio Sd15 Note

PublishedHardConstraints.description:
Represents the sections that mirror the API's rejections exactly.

A request honouring everything here cannot be one the API refuses on constraint grounds, which is
what separates these from the advisory sections.

rejected_sampler_scheduler_pairings.description: Pairings that produce no usable image and are refused rather than substituted.
rejected_sampler_scheduler_pairings.title: Rejected Sampler Scheduler Pairings

scheduler_baseline_applicability.description: Baselines each restricted scheduler is defined for. A scheduler absent here works on every baseline.
scheduler_baseline_applicability.title: Scheduler Baseline Applicability

PublishedHardConstraints.title: PublishedHardConstraints

PublishedKnobRange.description:
Represents the accepted range of one numeric solver knob, as it is served.

JSON has no literal for infinity, so an unbounded maximum, and a default meaning "the solver applies
no limit unless you set one", are both served as null rather than as a number.

maximum.description: Largest accepted value, inclusive. Null where the knob has no upper limit.
maximum.title: Maximum

default.description: The value the solver uses when the knob is left unset. Null where it applies no limit.
default.title: Default

integer_only.description: Whether the knob accepts only whole numbers.
integer_only.title: Integer Only

PublishedKnobRange.title: PublishedKnobRange

PublishedPresentationTiers.description: Represents the default-offer set, and the note saying the split restricts nothing.

note.description: States that every sampler is accepted, priced and dispatched identically whatever its tier.
note.title: Note

recommended.description: The samplers worth offering by default. Everything absent is advanced, not deprecated.
recommended.title: Recommended

PublishedPresentationTiers.title: PublishedPresentationTiers

PublishedRecommendation.description:
Represents one advisory statement, with the provenance that qualifies it.

Recommendations never block a request. The provenance is served because these range from statements
by the image backend's own author to third-party folklore, and a client cannot weigh them otherwise.

samplers.description: The samplers the statement applies to, empty when it applies to all of them.
samplers.title: Samplers

schedulers.description: The schedulers the statement recommends, empty when it recommends none.
schedulers.title: Schedulers

PublishedRecommendation.title: PublishedRecommendation

PublishedRejectedPairing.description: Represents one sampler and scheduler pairing the API refuses outright.

sampler.description: The sampler half of the refused pairing.

scheduler.description: The scheduler half of the refused pairing.

PublishedRejectedPairing.title: PublishedRejectedPairing

PublishedSamplerRecord.description: Represents one sampler's knobs, cost, tier and vocabulary as they are served.

name.description: The sampler this record describes, repeated here so an entry stands alone once read out of the map.

evaluations_per_step.description: How many model evaluations one step performs, which is what the API prices a request on.
evaluations_per_step.title: Evaluations Per Step

measured_cost_ratio_sd15.description:
Per-step wall-clock cost relative to `k_euler` on a stable_diffusion_1 model, or null where a ratio
is meaningless because the sampler chooses its own step count.
measured_cost_ratio_sd15.title: Measured Cost Ratio Sd15

measured_cost_ratio_sdxl.description: The same ratio on a stable_diffusion_xl model, or null for the same reason.
measured_cost_ratio_sdxl.title: Measured Cost Ratio Sdxl

presentation_tier.description: How prominently the sampler is worth offering. A presentation hint that restricts nothing.

solver_type_choices.description: The `solver_type` values this sampler accepts, empty when it takes none.
solver_type_choices.title: Solver Type Choices

accepted_settings.description:
The numeric knobs this sampler accepts, keyed by the request field name a client sends them under.

The keys are the serving API's own request field names rather than the knob names the backend's
solvers use, because a client reads this to build a request.
accepted_settings.title: Accepted Settings

applies_cfg_pp.description: Whether the sampler applies the CFG++ correction, which expects a much lower `cfg_scale`.
applies_cfg_pp.title: Applies Cfg Pp

PublishedSamplerRecord.title: PublishedSamplerRecord

SAMPLER_PRESENTATION_TIER.description:
How prominently a sampler is worth offering, now that the vocabulary is long enough to overwhelm.

This is a presentation concern and nothing else: every sampler here is accepted, priced and
dispatched identically whatever its tier. A client may default to showing only the recommended tier
and put the rest behind an "advanced" affordance, which is what the split is for.
SAMPLER_PRESENTATION_TIER.title: SAMPLER_PRESENTATION_TIER

description:
Represents the whole sampler constraints document an API serves.

Only samplers and schedulers the serving API accepts appear, so a client reading this never offers a
name that API's request models would reject as unknown.

Examples:
    Parsing a response from the sampler constraints endpoint:

    ```python
    document = SamplerConstraintsDocument.model_validate(response.json())
    euler = document.samplers[KNOWN_IMAGE_SAMPLERS.k_euler]
    ```
